rounds.text: Bajel Projects Ltd is demonstrating explosive fundamental acceleration that points directly to an under-appreciated turnaround story. Compounded sales growth has reached 61% over three years [E14], while compounded profit growth over the same period stands at an exceptional 125% [E16] alongside a massive 93% profit growth in the trailing twelve months [E17]. This earnings momentum is reinforced by a stellar net profit surge of 220% year-on-year [E58], supported by an operating margin that has expanded by 9 percentage points from -5% three years ago to 4% in March 2026 [E21] on a consistently increasing yearly trajectory [E23]. Furthermore, the company exhibits strong operating cash flow generation at Rs 21 Cr [E26], modest leverage with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.54x [E29], and a reduction in borrowings down to Rs 367 Cr from Rs 376 Cr a year prior [E30]. Conceded: [E36], [E37], [E38], [E63].

Bajel Projects Ltd trades at a steep P/E of 55.3x and a sector-beating 78.37x, while sitting at an elevated price-to-book of 3.04x [E1, E2, E6, E7]. This rich valuation is fundamentally disconnected from the company's weak profitability metrics, evidenced by an ROE of 4.1% and a low 3-year median ROE of 4% [E9, E19, E52]. The operational reality compounds these valuation risks, highlighted by high debtors of 214 days, a negative free cash flow of Rs -13 Cr, and operating cash flow constituting only 22% of operating profit in March 2026 [E27, E28, E53]. Institutional confidence is actively eroding, shown by a severe drop in foreign institutional holdings from 10.51% to 0.53% and domestic institutional holdings falling from 11.98% to 9.20% [E33, E34]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model suggests a major overvaluation with an intrinsic value of Rs 95 per share against a market price of Rs 179, requiring an aggressive 26.8% earnings growth rate that outpaces the base case assumption of 18.0% [E36, E38]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over 3 years is 61% and compounded profit growth over the same period is 125% [E14, E16].

Conceded: [E1], [E2], [E6], [E7], [E36], [E38]. While the bear highlights elevated valuation multiples, it ignores the powerful operating momentum that is currently outpacing those metrics, notably a 117% outperformance of profit growth over one-year price growth [E48]. The structural turnaround is unmistakable, as evidenced by a compounded sales growth of 61% over three years and compounded profit growth of 125% over the same period [E14, E16]. Operational efficiency is expanding rapidly rather than stagnating, with the yearly operating margin trend increasing over the last four years and delivering a 9 percentage point expansion to 4% in March 2026 [E21, E23]. Conceded: [E9], [E19], [E27], [E28], [E33], [E34], [E52], [E53]. Despite historical low returns on equity and institutional outflows, dismissing the company on stale sentiment overlooks that results are accelerating with recent quarterly net profit surging 220% year-on-year [E58, E64].

Conceded: [E14], [E16], [E21], [E23], [E58]. The bull relies heavily on past growth and surging short-term metrics to justify the valuation, but ignores the fundamental structural weakness revealed by a 3-year median return on equity of just 4% and a current ROE of 5.9% [E13, E19]. The argument that accelerating results outweigh historical concerns is directly countered by the fact that the company's free cash flow stood at a negative Rs 13 Cr in March 2026, with operating cash flow representing only 22% of operating profit [E27, E28]. Furthermore, the bull minimizes institutional exits, yet foreign and domestic institutions have drastically slashed their stakes from 10.51% and 11.98% down to 0.53% and 9.20% respectively [E33, E34]. This heavy institutional outflow and a negative money flow signal [E35] align with flags for high debtors of 214 days and a low interest coverage ratio [E51, E53], proving that the operational momentum touted by the bull masks deep cash generation and balance sheet vulnerabilities.
